Maya: FYI rolling nf4/fp4 kernel canary to ~5% traffic in us-west-2. Seeing a reproducible regression on small-batch (1-4) latency and a per-GPU RSS spike (~+1.1GB) within ~10m of traffic hitting the canary. dumping a few traces below. :frowning_face:

infra-bot: deploy started for canary nf4-fp4-canary-2026-03-18 by sasha

Maya: Perf sketch (p90 tokens/sec per-GPU): baseline nf4-old-kern: 1200 tok/s, canary nf4/fp4: 900 tok/s. Memory: baseline RSS 11.6GB, canary 12.8GB. Host-side memcpy stalls visible in logs.

Maya: quick log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-18 14:02:11] kernel_selector: chosen="quant4_opt_v2" reason="match:arch+seq>512"
[2026-03-18 14:02:11] runtime: small-batch path triggered, but kernel fallback->generic_gemm for matmul_1 due to alignment_miss
[2026-03-18 14:02:12] kvcache: alloc slab=hot_slab(256MB) -> fail, fallback to host_copy, memcpy 72ms
[2026-03-18 14:02:12] scheduler: prefetch_queue: enqueue_latency=4ms, dispatch_latency=18ms
```

Devon: can you paste the stackprof/pprof of the worker? also can you run the microbenchmark with --batch=1 --seq=128 and --pin-cpu? suspecting selector threshold misfires when seq distribution is skewed.

Maya: attaching quick flame (pasted inline): main hotspots are: quant4_matmul_slowpath (35%), host_memcpy (27%), selector_check (12%).

Sasha: hmm. we recently tweaked the selector vote for "prefers_packed_layout" to prefer quant4_opt_v2 when any tensor packed_ratio>0.6. that might be over-eager for small batches where packing overhead wins.

Ron: calibration note: the recent fp4 calibration introduced a per-layer extra reorder to satisfy block alignment for the gpu kernel. if the reorder runs on CPU for small batches it'll push us into host_copy path. did the canary include the reorder change?

Liam: yes, reorder landed in runtime/quant/calc_reorder PR #4121. it only triggers when layer dim%pad !=0 (we added pad to 64). small-batch with many short sequences can cause more layers to take the reorder.

Devon: hypothesis: selector votes + reorder => more layers choose quant4_opt_v2, but for some kernels runtime detects misaligned tensors and does host_copy fallback, causing memcpy and GC pressure. That explains the RSS bump and throughput drop.

Maya: agrees. quick test: flipping the selector threshold for packed_ratio from 0.6 -> 0.8 prevented the bad kernel from being chosen and restored baseline perf in a 10-min canary.

Sasha: can we get a reproducible unit test? try:
```bash
./tools/infer_bench --model-path=.../gpt-small-nf4 --batch=2 --seq=128 --pins=0-3 --samples=500 --use-cached-kv=false
```
This should surface the host_copy path quickly.

Devon: also run nvprof/cupti to check if kernels fall back to generic_gemm. run: `NVPROF_COMMAND=nvprof ./tools/infer_bench ...` and grep for "generic_gemm".

Ron: temporary mitigation plan: revert reorder or short-circuit selector for small-batch path. which one is lower risk? revert reorder touches calibration quality; selector tweak is runtime-only. I'd vote for runtime flag.

Liam: Agree. added feature-flag: runtime.config.use_packed_selector=true -> will flip to false for canary in prod. pushing patch now.

infra-bot: feature-flag updated: runtime.config.use_packed_selector=false for canary group id=0x3f

Maya: re-ran canary after flag flip: p90 tokens/sec back to ~1180, RSS back to 11.7GB. no memcpy spikes in the 15m window.

Sasha: good. next steps: 1) add a small-batch heuristic to selector (batch_size<=4 || seq<=64 -> prefer non-packed kernels), 2) add a unit test that covers packed_ratio edgecases, 3) run calibration sweep to ensure reorder removal doesn't regress accuracy.

Devon: logging follow-up: add a selector telemetry field with "vote_reason" and "alignment_check" booleans. also emit a telemetry event whenever host_copy fallback triggers with stack sample. saves hours.

Maya: assigning owners: selector heuristic & telemetry -> Devon, unit tests -> Sasha, calibration sweep & perf checks -> Ron. I'll coordinate canary ramp once fixes are in.

Liam: note: we'll also batch-merge a micro-optim that memaligns tensors to 64 on alloc to reduce alignment misses; running internal perf to confirm no overhead.

Devon: for the postmortem/slack thread, we'll capture: root cause (over-eager packed kernel selection + CPU reorder -> host_copy fallback), impact (p90 drop ~25%, RSS +1.1GB), mitigation (feature-flag flip), and long term (selector heuristics + allocator alignment).

Maya: thanks all. if anyone hits this outside the canary, ping and I'll flip the flag globally. :thumbsup:

Ron: noted, I'll start the calibration sweep tomorrow and post results in #eng-runtime.

Sasha: adding a quick gtest reproducer in PR; should be up by EOD.

Devon: adding telemetry TODO to infra backlog ticket INF-1029.

infra-bot: canary group 0x3f: runtime.config.use_packed_selector=false rolled to 100% (manual ramp)

Maya: closing loop here, leaving this thread for the postmortem notes. thanks everyone! :partyparrot:
